I’ve been farming this little plot for thirty years now — just 1.1 mu, barely enough to feed the family and bring in a bit of cash. My husband and two of the kids work off-farm in the county town, so it’s mostly me and my youngest daughter doing the field work. We’re not poor, but we’re not rich either. Every yuan I spend on inputs has to come from somewhere, so I don’t throw money around.

It’s October now, time to get the wheat in the ground. I saved about 8 kg of seed from last year — a local variety, nothing fancy, but it does fine on this soil. I’ll plant in the first week of October, same as always. For fertilizer, the extension fellow says I should use more, but I only have about 400 yuan set aside for the wheat season. I’ll buy two bags of compound fertilizer — that’s about 25 kg for the whole plot, so roughly 11 kg per mu split between base dressing and a little topdress at green-up. If the wheat looks yellow at jointing, I might add a splash of urea, but I’ll see how the money holds out. Water costs keep going up, so I’ll irrigate three times: once right after planting to get it germinated, once at wintering if it’s too dry, and once at jointing in spring. I can’t afford more pump hours than that.

Come June, the wheat should give me around 350 kg if the weather is decent. That’s not huge, but it’s enough for our flour and some to sell. The maize goes in the same day we finish cutting the wheat — there’s no time to waste. I usually plant the same local maize, but last year my nephew gave me some improved seed that did a bit better, so I’ll try that this time. For maize, I’ll put down about 10 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and if it rains well I might not need much else. I’ll irrigate once or twice — once at planting if it’s dry, and maybe once at flowering if the sky stays clear. I expect around 400 kg of maize, which goes to the pigs and some to market.

I don’t hire labor — it’s just us. The kids help during harvest and planting when they’re home, but mostly it’s me. My tools are old but they work. I till by hand hoe and a small rotary tiller I share with my brother-in-law.
